answer:
The energy eigenvalues for a 1D infinite potential box are given by $E_n = \frac{n^2 h^2}{8 m_e L^2}$. Given $L = 2.5 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}$, $m_e = 9.1 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$, $h = 6.64 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J.s}$.
For $n=1$ (Lowest energy $E_1$):
$E_1 = \frac{1^2 \times (6.64 \times 10^{-34})^2}{8 \times (9.1 \times 10^{-31}) \times (2.5 \times 10^{-10})^2} = 9.69 \times 10^{-20}\text{ J} = 0.605\text{ eV}$.
For $n=2$ ($E_2$):
$E_2 = 2^2 \times E_1 = 4 \times 9.69 \times 10^{-20} = 3.88 \times 10^{-19}\text{ J} = 2.42\text{ eV}$.
proTip: Always convert Joules to eV if required, by dividing the value in Joules by $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$.
